---
title: "Dual language immersion and the PPS rightsizing scenarios"
subtitle: "What Scenarios A and B (released October 2026) would change for immersion families"
toc: false
---

```{r}
source("R/site_data.R")

sp_k5 <- sites |> filter(language == "Spanish", band == "K-5", change != "removed" | is.na(change)) |> count(scenario)
moving_k5 <- moves |> filter(scenario == "a", band == "K-5", kind == "program")
moving_students <- moves |> filter(scenario == "a") |> rowwise() |>
  mutate(n = strand_students(from_key, language, band)) |> pull(n) |> sum()

sp_from <- moving_k5 |> filter(language == "Spanish") |> distinct(from_key)
sp_k <- lottery_k |> filter(language == "Spanish", year %in% LOTTERY_YEARS)
sp_share <- sum(sp_k$applications[sp_k$key %in% sp_from$from_key]) / sum(sp_k$applications)

acc <- read_data("access_summary.csv") |> filter(group == "Spanish (ages 5-17)")
acc_ci <- read_data("access_robustness_ci.csv")
```

Portland Public Schools (PPS) would move most of its **Spanish dual language immersion** (DLI) programs into fewer schools in both of its new scenarios. In these programs, students learn in two languages. In the two scenarios, A and B, PPS proposes to close or consolidate schools. PPS released them for the school board on October 6, 2026. Both scenarios also move or add Mandarin and Vietnamese sites. This site uses PPS's own enrollment and lottery reports to show what these changes mean for immersion families.

## What you will find on this site {#whats-here}

- **[Demand & scorecard](scorecard.qmd)**: how many families apply to each immersion program, compared with the schools the programs would move to. Then, for every language, the sites, students and pathways in each scenario.
- **[Equity](equity.qmd)**: the case for a different solution for immersion families. At the schools that would lose a program, about half the students are historically underserved. Closures fall mostly on whiter, higher-income schools. Some of the programs that would move have long waitlists. Past program moves lost families.
- **[Lent & César Chávez](history.qmd)**: the 2023 Bridger → Lent move, and César Chávez, the plan's new Spanish hub. The page covers 2019 through PPS's projections for 2031.
- **[Research](research.qmd)**: what published studies, field guidance and PPS's own Lent conversion show about whole-school versus strand immersion. In a whole-school program, every class is an immersion class. A strand is an immersion program inside a school that also has a neighborhood program. We found no study that compares the two on student outcomes.
- **[Sources & methods](methods.qmd)**: where every number comes from and what it can't tell you.

::: {.callout-note}
This is an independent analysis, not a PPS publication. We transcribed the scenario details from the October 2026 board packet. For the official versions, see the [PPS rightsizing materials](https://meetings.boardbook.org/Public/Agenda/915?meeting=769955).
:::
